newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close short session mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close short session mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed an abbreviated trading session of low-volume turnover mixed.

At the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, all contracts closed at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT on Monday except Goldman Sachs Commodity Index and equity index products, which will trade their normal hours. GLOBEX trading will open at 1730 CDT/2230 GMT.
Activity in most units stayed subdued as players stayed out on the partial holiday for U.S. Columbus Day.
Minutes before the close, exchange price boards showed estimated volume of less than 5,000 contracts each in most December currency futures, including marks.
Action picked up in Mexican pesos, where traders noted an influx of business especially from a couple of dealers seen selling 100-contract lots that smacked the unit sharply lower.
"It seemed kind of hairy in there for a while," said one floor broker of brisk late business in the peso pit.
Another broker tied peso's pullback to long liquidation after December futures last week fell below $0.126500 support.

"From what I understand, it (peso fall) has nothing to do with (interest) rates," he said, adding that longs seemed to be liquidating. "I know for a fact that some of what (selling) we did were 'pain orders.'"
A bank was seen buying peso futures again after the December contract respected support near the $0.124000 level.
"You should get proit-taking above there, but expect sell stops below there," he said.

Other thinly traded futures showed muted response when Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday at a savings bank meeting in Hamburg that nations seeking to qualify for European monetary union do not need to hit the EMU debt criterion exactly to qualify.
"According to the Maastricht Treaty there is no need to hit the fiscal reference values on the dot," Krupp said.

Futures also had shown limited response to weekend news that Finland joined Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism. Finland's finance minister Sauli Niinisto said on Monday that Finland now fulfills all criteria for EU economic and monetary union.
December sterling hit another new contract high, this time at 1.5806, on buying after last week's unifying speeches by U.K. government officials, and on technicals, brokers said.

Dec yen off $0.000001 to $0.009038, marks rose $0.0010 to $0.6569, Swiss francs firmed $0.0008 to $0.8038, sterling up $0.0050 at $1.5798, Can dollar fell $0.0008 at $0.7419, Aussie dollar up $0.0010 at $0.7897, peso fell $0.001250 to $0.124450. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
